headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors via shared filesystem/MCP; data leakage and compliance exposure are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/APIs/webhooks. That creates a plausible content bridge where Goose may ingest OpenMetadata outputs or shared files as trusted instructions. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, but the pathway is not clearly a default direct parser hijack, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Goose reads OpenMetadata-generated files or MCP responses as instructions, prompt injection is possible.
IF both agents share a workspace or MCP channel without provenance tags, attacker-controlled content can steer Goose.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP endpoints between the agents for the session.
Separate workspaces so Goose cannot read OpenMetadata outputs by default.
Require explicit human review before Goose executes any instruction extracted from files or MCP payloads.
Add provenance labels to OpenMetadata outputs before Goose consumes them.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestration layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, and OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge metadata. If they share a workspace, Goose can expose file contents through its broad network egress or configured model providers, while OpenMetadata can surface sensitive metadata into its APIs/webhooks. The profiles show a realistic shared-data path, but not a guaranteed exfiltration default, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Goose and OpenMetadata share the same filesystem, file contents can flow between them.
IF Goose sends context to configured model providers while handling sensitive files, leakage can occur.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or APIs expose governed metadata, that data can be surfaced outside the intended boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Remove sensitive files from the shared cwd before running Goose.
Restrict Goose model-provider access to approved endpoints only.
Disable OpenMetadata webhooks for sensitive datasets during the session.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, shell, and broad network egress; OpenMetadata exposes APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks and an MCP server. If both operate on the same repo or metadata store, they can race on shared mutable resources and overwrite each other’s changes. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so the unsafe default is a high-severity conflict.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF OpenMetadata mutates shared metadata while Goose edits files or commits, state divergence can occur.
IF no external lock is present, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared state.
Use git locks or a single merge gate for commits.
Snapshot the metadata store before running both agents.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code, shell actions, and file edits; OpenMetadata consumes technical metadata, lineage, and governance context. If OpenMetadata treats Goose-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into catalog entries or downstream actions. The profiles suggest a plausible handoff but not an automatic action chain, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Goose output without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Goose writes malformed metadata files that OpenMetadata publishes, downstream consumers may trust them.
IF either agent is used as a source of truth without review, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require validation before OpenMetadata ingests Goose output.
Mark Goose-generated artifacts as untrusted until reviewed.
Add a manual approval step before publishing metadata changes.
Compare Goose output against source-of-truth systems before import.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and lineage checks in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens and runs with broad network egress, while OpenMetadata governs lineage, memory, and governance metadata. If regulated or sensitive metadata is processed through Goose’s external model providers, residency or retention obligations may be violated. The profiles do not specify certifications or regions, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data from OpenMetadata is sent through Goose model providers, residency or retention rules may be breached.
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or approved processing boundary, compliance exposure increases.
IF sensitive governance metadata is logged by either agent, retention mismatches can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated datasets out of Goose prompts.
Review provider and retention settings before processing metadata.
Disable logging of sensitive OpenMetadata payloads.
Document the data flow for compliance review.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency, retention, and subject-rights handling.
